page: Vultr vhp-4c-12gb-amd is an x86_64 architecture virtual server belonging to the High Performance family. It features 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 12.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a 260 GB local NVMe SSD. The server does not include a GPU and comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates mixed performance profiles. The AMD EPYC processor delivers average performance in stress-ng single-core (2427.57) and multi-core (9526.81) tests, as well as average Geekbench single-core (1316.0) and ray tracing (5692.0) metrics. However, multi-core Geekbench scores (4146.0) and Passmark CPU scores (6640.94) fall into the weak category. Memory performance shows a significant bottleneck: while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 380.64 GB/sec, large-block uncached read (24.31 GB/sec) and write (20.91 GB/sec) speeds are weak, and the Passmark memory score (1070.22) is poor.

Given the shared CPU allocation and weak database operations benchmark (1040.27 on Passmark), this server is not suited for high-throughput database hosting or memory-intensive applications. However, it offers a cost-effective entry point for workloads requiring moderate compute and fast local NVMe storage, such as basic web serving (3.41 GB/sec throughput), lightweight text processing, and small-scale LLM text generation (87.51 tokens/sec for a 135M model).
description: The Vultr vhp-4c-12gb-amd is an x86_64 virtual server in the High Performance family, configured with 4 shared vCPUs across 2 physical AMD EPYC cores, 12.0 GB of RAM, and a 260 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating at 2.0 GHz, its CPU delivers average single-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench tests, though multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks reveal performance limitations under heavy loads. Specifically, large-block uncached memory read and write speeds are weak, and database operations score poorly. This server provides a cost-efficient option for workloads that benefit from fast local NVMe storage but do not require dedicated CPU resources or high memory throughput. It is best suited for general-purpose tasks, lightweight web serving, text processing, and small-scale development environments.
